newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila frees opposition leader Tshisekedi.
newsitem.headline: Kabila frees opposition leader Tshisekedi.

text.p: Veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi was released on Friday, the morning after soldiers from Laurent Kabila's army arrested him at his home, a senior aide said.
Tshisekedi, members of his family and other associates had been taken away late on Thursday, hours after he addressed several thousand students in defiance of a government ban on political activity.
Adrien Phongo, secretary general of Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party, told Reuters that those arrested had been released on Friday.
"He was questioned for a long time. We are disappointed. They want to light the fire," Phongo said.

Tshisekedi was the main domestic opponent to veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, whom Kabila and his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo toppled in May after a seven-month civil war.
Witnesses said the arrest triggered protests by Tshisekedi loyalists who set fire to at least four vehicles in his Limete district of the capital Kinshasa.

Tshisekedi, named prime minister by a national democracy conference but sacked by Mobutu, was a constant thorn in the side of the veteran dictator. He never accepted his sacking and his supporters still refer to him as the prime minister.
Kabila has banned political parties, marches and gatherings and has alienated opposition followers by excluding Tshisekedi from his new government.
"It's the opening shot of a civil war. We fear for his life. They could easily poison him," the detained leader's adviser Mukendi wa Mulumba told Reuters after the arrest.
Kabila's ban on politics has undermined support for the man who was seen as a hero for ending Mobutu's 32-year corrupt rule.

Kabila indicated recently he would crack down on those who flouted the decree after turning a blind eye to several pro-Tshisekedi marches in the capital Kinshasa. Kabila soldiers broke up earlier marches with teargas or by firing in the air.
Ironically, Tshisekedi's address to thousands of students at the city university had been full of conciliatory messages.
He announced that he had held talks with Kabila's Alliance movement to "harmonize conflicting views" on the institutions of the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Tshisekedi said his new contacts with the Alliance could lead to a new transitional government to prepare for elections promised for 1999, and that he could soon meet Kabila for the first time since he declared himself president.
"We gave a message of appeasement and they have answered that with force," adviser Mukendi said after the arrest.
The teeming city of Kinshasa is a hotbed of support for the veteran opposition leader and his now officially suspended UDPS party.
A government spokesman said earlier he was unaware of the arrest. It is unclear whether the government would take the matter further or what punishment defying the ban could entail.
